title: Lifting the locus of a power of one section through a square-zero immersion
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], both locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $\mathcal I=j.\ker$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] satisfy $\mathcal I^2=0$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Let $\mathcal L$ be invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], put $N=j^*\mathcal L$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and take any $n\geq0$ and $s\in\Gamma(Z,N^{\otimes n})$. Suppose an affine open $U\subset Z$ has underlying set exactly the nonvanishing locus $Z_s$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then there are an integer $k>0$ and a section $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes nk})$ such that, for every $z\in Z$, $t$ is nonzero in the fibre at $j(z)$ if and only if $z\in U$. In particular $j^{-1}(X_t)=U$ as sets. No ampleness is assumed, and no affineness of $X_t$ is asserted.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Apply the section-power lift to obtain k>0, t, and e. The pullback of L is invertible by the invertible-pullback-tensor theorem, as are its tensor powers.

Convert the pulled-back section and s to complements of zero-locus supports using the nonvanishing dictionary. Hom.zeroLocus_eq_of_arrowIso removes the module isomorphism e from the equality supplied by the lift. The proved upstream compl_support_zeroLocus_tensorPowSection (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.AffineComplement) identifies the zero-locus support of the positive tensor power with that of the original section.

For each z, the nonvanishing tensor-pullback criterion identifies nonvanishing of t at j(z) with nonvanishing of its restricted section at z. Combine with the preceding equality of loci and the given hU.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 09MS, section-power lift followed by equality of nonvanishing sets
proof_origin.note: T1 second reader: real section-power lifting reduction, with the locus argument proved using existing zero-locus and pullback declarations.

lean.statement: theorem exists_section_power_locus_of_square_zero {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [CompactSpace X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Z] [CompactSpace Z] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥) (n : ℕ) (s : (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) (U : Z.Opens) (hU : (U : Set Z) = nonvanishingLocus (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n) s) (hAffine : IsAffineOpen U) : ∃ k : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ ∃ t : (L.tensorPow (n * k)).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤), ∀ z : Z, j z ∈ nonvanishingLocus (L.tensorPow (n * k)) t ↔ z ∈ U
